fr:title.text: Latest Status on Extraction of Parsers to Haskell

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Latest Status on Extraction of Parsers to Haskell

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Revived parser extraction on a new extraction-no-glue branch in the gsa-extraction worktree. End-to-end runDyck.sh now produces a working 30 MB MAlonzo-compiled Haskell binary that correctly accepts/rejects Dyck-bracket inputs.
Phase A — seed + drift fixes — is done. The branch currently sits as three commits above main:

html:ul.html:li: Seed from extraction_demo (squashed) — overlayed extraction_demo's src/ tree onto extraction-no-glue.
Phase A drift fixes — reconciled the tree with current agda 2.9 and the pinned cubical at .libs/cubical.
runDyck.sh rewrite — uses --library-file pointing at .agda-config/libraries so the build is hermetic.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Concrete drift that had to be fixed before anything typechecked:

html:ul.html:li: --guardedness is infective from cubical, added to grammar.agda-lib.
agda-stdlib 2.2 is incompatible with agda 2.9 (unrecognized --warn=noUserWarning). Dropped the dep entirely and inlined the three functions that needed it: _==_, show, intersperse.
Cubical.Data.Sum.More clashed with cubical-categorical-logic — renamed local copy to Cubical.Data.Sum.Extra.
Cubical.Data.FinSet.More and Cubical.Relation.Nullary.DecidablePropositions.More had definitions that drifted into pinned cubical — added hiding clauses.
Under --erased-cubical, Path refl is erased, so postulates had to switch from Path _≡_ to Eq._≡_ with Eq.refl.
IO used to come from the stdlib — wrote a tiny local src/IO.agda wrapping Agda.Builtin.IO with COMPILE GHC pragmas.

fr:mainmatter.html:pre: [][[]] → inl(bal(literal([), nil, literal(]), bal(literal([), bal(literal([), nil, literal(]), nil), literal(]), nil))) [[[[]]]] → full 4-level nested parse tree [[ → inr(reject) (empty) → inl(nil)
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The extracted Haskell lives at gsa-extraction/src/MAlonzo/MAlonzo/Code/ (139 .hs files, 7.5 MB of generated source); the binary is at gsa-extraction/src/MAlonzo/Dyck.
Why extraction_demo ever worked in the first place — the trick is a five-layer stack:

html:ol.html:li: --erased-cubical drops cubical primitives at compile time.
@0 runtime-irrelevance annotations on path-flavoured definitions so they never reach the extractor.
SplittingEq carries an inductive Eq._≡_ inside _⊗_'s runtime data instead of a cubical Path, so pattern-matching on Eq.refl needs no primTransp.
Parallel AsPath/ and AsEquality/ module trees per connective, with Base.agda re-exporting the Eq version so runtime code transparently uses the non-path variant.
A hand-ported Erased/Data/* subtree of cubical-free reimplementations of the stdlib modules that MAlonzo actually wants to compile.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Phase B (collapsing Splitting to be Eq-only and deleting the parallel AsPath//AsEquality/ module trees) was intentionally deferred. Extraction already works end-to-end with the parallel trees in place, and the cleanup is a pure maintainability win rather than a blocker, so it can wait until there's a concrete reason to revisit String/Base.agda and Grammar/LinearProduct/Base.agda.

Added two new REPL modes to Examples/Dyck.agda — (g) for linearly-generated balanced strings without parsing, and (h) for linearly-generated unbalanced strings without parsing. Running these side-by-side with the existing end-to-end modes (3) and (7) isolates generation cost from parsing cost. Benchmarks were taken on the extracted Dyck binary (src/MAlonzo/Dyck, ~30 MB, Apple M-series arm64) via /usr/bin/time -l, piping input into the REPL so the timing captures startup + menu + generation + parse + print. Every row is a single cold run (no warm-up), so low-N numbers are dominated by RTS startup.
Wall-clock time (seconds), peak resident set size in MiB, and a derived parse-only column computed as end_to_end - gen_only:

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: GHC RTS breakdown at N = 1,000,000 balanced

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Captured with +RTS -s -RTS on mode 3 and mode g:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: end-to-end (3) gen-only (g) bytes allocated 8.51 GB 553 MB bytes copied (GC) 1.10 GB 46.3 KB max residency 192.0 MB 17.2 MB total memory 454 MiB 38 MiB Gen-0 collections 2,031 119 Gen-1 collections 10 6 MUT time 1.236 s 0.081 s GC time 0.693 s 0.026 s Total time 1.940 s 0.110 s Productivity 63.7 % 73.6 % Alloc rate 6.89 GB / MUT-s 6.84 GB / MUT-s

html:ul.html:li: Parsing dominates. At every size past ~100k characters, generation is well under 10 percent of the wall time; the rest is the DFA trace construction + the final mkTree pass. At N = 3.45 M the split is ~94 percent parse / ~6 percent gen.
Linear in N. End-to-end wall time tracks N almost exactly: ~2 μs per N-step over the whole range, i.e. ~0.5 μs per input character. No super-linear blow-up up to 8 M N (32 M characters).

Memory is the real ceiling. End-to-end RSS is ~215 bytes per character — the parser holds the full input list plus the intermediate trace + Dyck tree in live heap. At 8 M N that's ~3 GB. The interactive 3.45 M ceiling you hit is the point where this machine starts feeling it, not a parser-side bug. Generation-only memory is ~9 bytes per character, confirming that Haskell laziness streams the list just fine when nothing downstream is forcing random access.

GC pressure is high but survivable. Productivity at N = 1 M end-to-end is 63.7 percen (2,041 total GCs, 35.7 percent GC time), vs. 73.6 percent for generation only. Allocation rate is ~6.9 GB/MUT-s in both modes, but the parse path copies 1.1 GB during GC vs. 46 KB for gen-only — the intermediate Trace/Dyck structures have short lifetimes and churn through the nursery aggressively.

Balanced vs unbalanced is indistinguishable. The linear unbalanced generator puts the mismatch at the very end of the string, so the parser chews through essentially the same amount of work as the balanced case before hitting the rejecting branch of parseDyck. Same wall time, same RSS to within noise.
Small-N floor is ~30 ms. Below N ≈ 10 k the runtime is dominated by GHC RTS startup, binary load, and REPL I/O, so low-N entries are only useful as a baseline for overhead.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Next steps if/when this comes back up:

html:ul.html:li: Port the other example parsers (BinOp, RegexParser) the same way and confirm they extract.
Decide whether Phase B is worth doing before merging extraction-no-glue back toward main, or whether the branch stays as an extraction-only side-branch.
Think about a real IO layer beyond the tiny src/IO.agda shim — the current one only exposes putStrLn/getLine.

Investigate whether a streaming parse (avoiding the full intermediate tree) could cut the ~215 bytes/char memory constant and push the interactive ceiling past 10 M without raising the machine's RSS watermark.
